acceptance: Red first: a clean tree with a merged branch and a clean tree with a closed unmerged branch are removed through `evolve gc`, and each branch stays
Red first: a dirty tree is kept and the report lists its changed paths
Red first: a tree that matches gc.dev_worktrees.protected stays and the reason names the glob; no code list holds code-index
Red first: a tree with a process inside or an open pull request stays
The dry run on the 2026-11-22 fixture shape (98 trees, 35 clean landed) lists the keep reason of each tree
New code at 100% measured coverage of the changed functions; one end-to-end test through the real verb
fix: In the dev sweep add the closed state to landedEarly: a clean tree with no process inside and a branch that is merged, closed or in origin/main is removed after the existing checkpoint save, and the branch stays. Report a dirty tree with its changed paths and never remove it in this rule. Add gc.dev_worktrees.protected, a list of globs relative to the dev dir (start value code-index), kept with the reason 'protected by policy: <glob>'. Build step 1 prints the keep reason of each tree of the live hub in dry run, to find which gate kept the 35.
summary: Plan docs/plans/cycle-recycle-and-gc-check-2026-11.md section 13, decisions D24 to D26, component X12. The console dev dirs held 22 GB in 119 directories on 2026-11-22 (operator). The sweep only listed them: '0 of 98 idle past the archive limit'. The console removed 35 clean trees with a merged or closed pull request by hand (6 GB); 39 dirty trees hold uncommitted source. The dev sweep removes a tree only when idle 14 days or landed early (devlanded.go:14-36); a CLOSED pull request is not a case, a dirty tree has no path list, and only the project root and plane worktrees are protected, by code (devworktrees.go:219-227).
title: gc removes a clean landed or closed console dev worktree, reports a dirty one with its paths, and protects named trees by policy data
